title: Estimate a causal effect using DAG-guided backdoor adjustment — causal_estimate_effect
code: if (requireNamespace("dagitty", quietly = TRUE)) {   dag <- causal_cerrado_dag()    # Greenness looks like an enormous SOC driver until the DAG is   # honoured: twi, slope and map_mm cause both ndvi and soc, so the   # raw slope (about 49) is inflated. Adjusting cuts it to about 18.   print(causal_estimate_effect(br_cerrado, dag, "ndvi", "soc"))    # Elevation is the instructive case: the adjusted effect comes out   # positive, the unadjusted one negative -- a sign flip.   print(causal_estimate_effect(br_cerrado, dag, "elev", "soc"))    # Read that flip carefully. elev has no parents in this DAG, so   # the unadjusted slope is not confounded at all, despite the   # wording the print method uses: it is the *total* effect, and   # asking for it reproduces the naive number exactly. The gap   # between the two is mediation through slope, twi and map_mm.   print(dagitty::parents(dag, "elev"))   print(causal_estimate_effect(br_cerrado, dag, "elev", "soc",                                effect = "total"))    # Same adjustment set, non-linear estimator. BART also puts the   # direct elevation effect above zero, and lands below the OLS   # slope. Note what it reports: an average finite difference over a   # step of delta = IQR/2 (76.4 m of elevation here), not a local   # derivative, so it equals the OLS coefficient only if the   # response really is linear over that span.   if (requireNamespace("dbarts", quietly = TRUE)) {     set.seed(1)     print(causal_estimate_effect(       br_cerrado, dag, "elev", "soc", estimator = "bart",       bart_kwargs = list(ntree = 50L, ndpost = 200L, nskip = 100L)))   } } #> <edaphos_causal_effect> #>   ndvi -> soc   (estimator: lm) #>   adjustment set : {map_mm, slope, twi} #>   direct effect  : 18.43   (95% CI: 14.61, 22.25) #>   naive effect   : 49.36   (un-adjusted, likely confounded) #> <edaphos_causal_effect> #>   elev -> soc   (estimator: lm) #>   adjustment set : {map_mm, slope, twi} #>   direct effect  : 0.01482   (95% CI: 0.01048, 0.01916) #>   naive effect   : -0.02389   (un-adjusted, likely confounded) #> character(0) #> <edaphos_causal_effect> #>   elev -> soc   (estimator: lm) #>   adjustment set : {(empty)} #>   total effect   : -0.02389   (95% CI: -0.02627, -0.02152) #>   naive effect   : -0.02389   (un-adjusted, likely confounded) #> <edaphos_causal_effect> #>   elev -> soc   (estimator: bart) #>   adjustment set : {map_mm, slope, twi} #>   direct effect  : 0.01007   (95% credible: 0.004576, 0.01475) #>   naive effect   : -0.02389   (un-adjusted, likely confounded) #>   delta (finite diff) : 76.4

code: # Relevance is the one IV assumption the data can actually check, # so run the first stage before trusting any 2SLS point estimate. set.seed(42) n <- 300 mgmt      <- rnorm(n) carbonate <- runif(n, 0, 12)   # parent-rock CaCO3, per cent quarry_km <- runif(n, 1, 60)   # distance to the nearest lime quarry clay      <- rnorm(n, 35, 8)   # exogenous control that also drives pH ph <- 4.6 + 0.10 * carbonate - 0.010 * quarry_km + 0.06 * clay +       0.45 * mgmt + rnorm(n, 0, 0.25) soil <- data.frame(ph, carbonate, quarry_km, clay,                    rainfall_resid = rnorm(n))  fs <- causal_iv_first_stage(soil, exposure = "ph",                             instruments = c("carbonate", "quarry_km"),                             covariates = "clay") c(F = fs$F, R2 = fs$R2, R2_partial = fs$R2_partial) #>          F         R2 R2_partial  #> 80.9710469  0.5787263  0.3536301   # F = 81 clears the Stock-Yogo rule of thumb by a wide margin. The # rule is not a significance test: F = 10 is roughly where 2SLS # bias back towards OLS, and under-coverage of the nominal 95 per # cent interval, stop being negligible. fs$F > 10 #> [1] TRUE  # The trap: `R2` scores the WHOLE first stage, controls included, # so it stays respectable even when the instruments are worthless. # Replacing them with noise leaves R2 at 0.35 -- down from 0.58, but # still the sort of number that reads as "the model fits", and all # of it carried by clay. F and the partial R2 do not survive the # substitution at all: 81 -> 0.33 and 0.354 -> 0.001. A drop of # 40 per cent against drops of 245x and 320x is the whole point -- # only `R2_partial` and `F` speak to identification. bad <- causal_iv_first_stage(soil, exposure = "ph",                              instruments = "rainfall_resid",                              covariates = "clay") c(F = bad$F, R2 = bad$R2, R2_partial = bad$R2_partial) #>           F          R2  R2_partial  #> 0.330165277 0.348970414 0.001110433   # `full_fit` is the fitted lm, so the individual first-stage slopes # can be signed against agronomy: carbonate raises pH, distance to # the quarry lowers it. coef(fs$full_fit) #>  (Intercept)         clay    carbonate    quarry_km  #>  4.638072937  0.057186405  0.103831703 -0.009107511

title: Two-stage least squares (2SLS) instrumental variable estimator — causal_iv_fit_2sls
text: Let X endogenous exposure (one column), Z matrix instruments, W matrix exogenous controls (included stages). Define augmented matrices X_all = [W, X] Z_all = [W, Z] projection P = Z_all (Z_all' Z_all)^-1 Z_all'.  2SLS estimator $$\hat{\beta} = (X_{\text{}}^\top P X_{\text{}})^{-1} X_{\text{}}^\top P Y$$ residuals computed using ORIGINAL X_all, first-stage fitted values, $$\hat{\sigma}^2 = (Y - X_{\text{}} \hat{\beta})^\top (Y - X_{\text{}} \hat{\beta}) / (n - k)$$ $$\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat{\beta}) = \hat{\sigma}^2 (X_{\text{}}^\top P X_{\text{}})^{-1}$$ Identification conditions (Wooldridge 2010, section 5.1): Relevance: \(\mathrm{rank}(Z' X) = \dim(X)\); first-stage F-statistic exceed 10 (Stock & Yogo 2005). Exclusion: \(Z\) affects \(Y\) \(X\). Unconfoundedness: \(Z \perp U\) \(U\) unobserved confounder.

title: Two-stage least squares (2SLS) instrumental variable estimator — causal_iv_fit_2sls
code: # A liming study confounded by management: unobserved agronomic # intensity raises both soil pH and yield, so no regression of # yield on pH can identify the causal effect. set.seed(42) n <- 300 mgmt      <- rnorm(n)          # unobserved agronomic intensity carbonate <- runif(n, 0, 12)   # parent-rock CaCO3, per cent quarry_km <- runif(n, 1, 60)   # distance to the nearest lime quarry ph    <- 4.6 + 0.10 * carbonate - 0.010 * quarry_km +          0.45 * mgmt + rnorm(n, 0, 0.25) yield <- 1.0 + 1.5 * ph + 1.3 * mgmt + rnorm(n, 0, 0.4) soil  <- data.frame(ph, yield, carbonate, quarry_km)  # The true effect is 1.5 t/ha per pH unit. OLS returns 2.85 -- # nearly double -- because it credits pH with the yield that # management delivered. ols <- lm(yield ~ ph, data = soil) coef(ols)[["ph"]] #> [1] 2.852879  # 2SLS uses only the pH variation forced by geology, which # management cannot touch: 1.62, with a 95 per cent interval that # covers 1.5. fit <- causal_iv_fit_2sls(soil, exposure = "ph", outcome = "yield",                           instruments = c("carbonate", "quarry_km")) fit #> <edaphos_causal_iv> #>   ph -> yield  (estimator: 2SLS, n = 300) #>   instruments : carbonate, quarry_km #>   effect      : 1.6161  (se = 0.1758, 95% CI [1.2715, 1.9606]) #>   stage-1 F   : 116.23 (p = 5.18e-38)  partial R^2 = 0.439 #>   Sargan J    : chi2(1) = 0.27, p = 0.604  # Consistency is bought with variance: the IV standard error here # is about twice the OLS one. Quoting the narrow OLS interval # around the wrong number is what this estimator exists to avoid. c(ols = summary(ols)$coefficients["ph", "Std. Error"], iv = fit$se) #>        ols         iv  #> 0.09183934 0.17579015   # `effect` is the exposure coefficient alone; `coefs` carries the # whole second-stage vector and `vcov` its 2SLS covariance -- not # the naive lm() covariance of a regression on fitted values. fit$coefs #> intercept        ph  #> 0.4044785 1.6160522  sqrt(diag(fit$vcov)) #> intercept        ph  #> 0.8615058 0.1757901

title: Fit 2SLS using foundation-model (or proxy) embeddings as instruments — causal_iv_from_embeddings
code: # Patch embeddings as candidate instruments. Only four of the # twelve dimensions track the parent material; the other eight # track canopy, which carries no geology at all. set.seed(11) n <- 300 mgmt      <- rnorm(n) carbonate <- runif(n, 0, 12) quarry_km <- runif(n, 1, 60) ph    <- 4.6 + 0.10 * carbonate - 0.010 * quarry_km +          0.45 * mgmt + rnorm(n, 0, 0.25) yield <- 1.0 + 1.5 * ph + 1.3 * mgmt + rnorm(n, 0, 0.4) soil  <- data.frame(ph, yield)  canopy <- rnorm(n) emb <- cbind(   matrix(canopy, n, 8)           + matrix(rnorm(n * 8, 0, 0.5), n),   matrix(scale(carbonate), n, 2) + matrix(rnorm(n * 2, 0, 0.5), n),   matrix(scale(quarry_km), n, 2) + matrix(rnorm(n * 2, 0, 0.5), n) ) colnames(emb) <- paste0("emb_", 1:12)  # The trap: prcomp ranks components by variance in the EMBEDDING, # not by relevance to the exposure. PC_1 holds 0.56 of that # variance and is pure canopy, so on its own it is a # non-instrument: F = 0.03 and an interval from -13.5 to +19.4. causal_iv_from_embeddings(soil, emb, "ph", "yield", n_pcs = 1L) #> <edaphos_causal_iv> #>   ph -> yield  (estimator: 2SLS, n = 300) #>   instruments : PC_1 #>   effect      : 2.9526  (se = 8.4082, 95% CI [-13.5272, 19.4324]) #>   stage-1 F   : 0.03 (p = 0.852)  partial R^2 = 0.000 #>   [warning] Stock-Yogo threshold F < 10; instruments may be weak.  # Three PCs reach the geology directions: F = 45.6, and the # interval [0.87, 1.75] covers the true effect of 1.5. causal_iv_from_embeddings(soil, emb, "ph", "yield", n_pcs = 3L) #> <edaphos_causal_iv> #>   ph -> yield  (estimator: 2SLS, n = 300) #>   instruments : PC_1, PC_2, PC_3 #>   effect      : 1.3124  (se = 0.2251, 95% CI [0.8713, 1.7535]) #>   stage-1 F   : 45.55 (p = 3.12e-24)  partial R^2 = 0.316 #>   Sargan J    : chi2(2) = 0.19, p = 0.908  # More PCs is not monotonically better. The default n_pcs = 5L buys # extra Sargan degrees of freedom but dilutes the joint first-stage # F, which tests a growing number of restrictions: it falls from # 45.6 at three PCs to 27.9 at five while the estimate barely # moves. Choose n_pcs on the first stage, not on a default. sapply(1:5, function(k)   causal_iv_from_embeddings(soil, emb, "ph", "yield",                             n_pcs = k)$stage1_F) #> [1]  0.03498204  7.33208490 45.54941709 34.56315589 27.93657446  # `pca_variance_explained` documents the choice, but read it as an # audit trail rather than a relevance ranking -- PC_1 dominates it # and is the one component that identifies nothing. fit <- causal_iv_from_embeddings(soil, emb, "ph", "yield", n_pcs = 3L) round(fit$pca_variance_explained, 3) #>   PC1   PC2   PC3  #> 0.560 0.153 0.147   # Constant embedding dimensions are dropped before PCA rather than # breaking `scale. = TRUE`; `embedding_cols` records what survived. length(causal_iv_from_embeddings(soil, cbind(emb, dead_dim = 1),                                  "ph", "yield",                                  n_pcs = 3L)$embedding_cols) #> [1] 12

code: # Geology is a landscape attribute, so the instruments are constant # within a farm -- and the agronomy shock is shared within a farm # too. That is the regime where row-wise resampling lies. set.seed(7) n_farm     <- 40 farm       <- rep(seq_len(n_farm), each = 8) farm_shock <- rnorm(n_farm, 0, 1.2)[farm]   # shared agronomy carbonate  <- runif(n_farm, 0, 12)[farm]    # parent-rock CaCO3 quarry_km  <- runif(n_farm, 1, 60)[farm]    # km to the lime quarry n     <- length(farm) mgmt  <- rnorm(n) ph    <- 4.6 + 0.10 * carbonate - 0.010 * quarry_km +          0.45 * mgmt + rnorm(n, 0, 0.25) yield <- 1.0 + 1.5 * ph + 1.3 * mgmt + farm_shock + rnorm(n, 0, 0.4) soil  <- data.frame(ph, yield, carbonate, quarry_km, farm)  # Resampling rows pretends the 320 plots are 320 independent draws. iv_rows <- causal_iv_posterior(   soil, "ph", "yield", instruments = c("carbonate", "quarry_km"),   B = 150L, seed = 1, units = "t/ha per pH unit")  # Resampling farms respects the level at which the instruments and # the shock actually vary. iv_farms <- causal_iv_posterior(   soil, "ph", "yield", instruments = c("carbonate", "quarry_km"),   B = 150L, cluster = "farm", seed = 1, units = "t/ha per pH unit")  # The cluster bootstrap is about twice as wide, 0.48 against 0.23. # The analytic 2SLS standard error, 0.22, agrees with the row # bootstrap and is just as wrong: neither knows the effective # sample size is 40 farms, not 320 plots. fit <- causal_iv_fit_2sls(soil, "ph", "yield",                           instruments = c("carbonate", "quarry_km")) c(analytic = fit$se, boot_rows = iv_rows$sd, boot_farms = iv_farms$sd) #>   analytic  boot_rows boot_farms  #>  0.2201736  0.2332016  0.4827354   # The centre barely moves: clustering is about uncertainty, not # about bias. Both results are ordinary edaphos_posterior objects. iv_farms #> <edaphos_posterior> #>   method      : bootstrap #>   query_type  : effect #>   units       : t/ha per pH unit #>   n_samples   : 150 #>   query shape : 1 #>   mean range  : [+1.7026, +1.7026]  mean = +1.7026 #>   sd   range  : [+0.4827, +0.4827]  mean = +0.4827 c(rows = iv_rows$mean, farms = iv_farms$mean) #>     rows    farms  #> 1.649371 1.702640   # Resamples that fail to fit are dropped silently, so check how # many draws actually survived before quoting an interval. iv_farms$metadata$B #> [1] 150

title: Sargan test for instrument over-identification — causal_iv_sargan_test
text: $$J = n \cdot R^2_{uu}$$ R^2_uu R-squared regressing 2SLS residuals instruments (controls).  H0, J ~ chi-sq(L - K) L number instruments K number endogenous regressors.  Rejection (p < 0.05) evidence least one instrument invalid.

title: Sargan test for instrument over-identification — causal_iv_sargan_test
code: # `carb_direct` and `quarry_direct` let an instrument reach yield # WITHOUT going through pH, i.e. break the exclusion restriction. sim_liming <- function(seed = 42, carb_direct = 0,                        quarry_direct = 0) {   set.seed(seed)   n <- 300   mgmt      <- rnorm(n)   carbonate <- runif(n, 0, 12)   quarry_km <- runif(n, 1, 60)   ph    <- 4.6 + 0.10 * carbonate - 0.010 * quarry_km +            0.45 * mgmt + rnorm(n, 0, 0.25)   yield <- 1.0 + 1.5 * ph + 1.3 * mgmt + rnorm(n, 0, 0.4) +            carb_direct * carbonate + quarry_direct * quarry_km   data.frame(ph, yield, carbonate, quarry_km) } soil <- sim_liming()  # The test needs MORE instruments than endogenous exposures. One # instrument for one exposure is exactly identified: there is # nothing to over-identify, and you get NA rather than a # reassuring p-value. causal_iv_sargan_test(soil, "ph", "yield", instruments = "carbonate") #> $stat #> [1] NA #>  #> $df #> [1] 0 #>  #> $p #> [1] NA #>   # Two instruments, both valid by construction: J = 0.27 on 1 df, # p = 0.60, no evidence against the exclusion restriction. causal_iv_sargan_test(soil, "ph", "yield",                       instruments = c("carbonate", "quarry_km")) #> $stat #> [1] 0.2685378 #>  #> $df #> [1] 1 #>  #> $p #> [1] 0.6043143 #>   # Let carbonate fertilise the crop directly, breaking exclusion for # that instrument only. The two instruments now disagree about the # effect and the test fires: J = 19.6, p = 9.4e-06. causal_iv_sargan_test(sim_liming(carb_direct = 0.15), "ph", "yield",                       instruments = c("carbonate", "quarry_km")) #> $stat #> [1] 19.63545 #>  #> $df #> [1] 1 #>  #> $p #> [1] 9.371428e-06 #>   # What a non-rejection does NOT prove. Break BOTH instruments in # proportion to their first-stage strength and they agree on the # same wrong answer, so Sargan sees no conflict (p = 0.92) while # 2SLS returns 2.93 against a truth of 1.5. The J-statistic # compares instruments with each other; a bias they share is # invisible to it, and no over-identification test can license the # exclusion restriction on its own. soil_worse <- sim_liming(carb_direct = 0.15, quarry_direct = -0.015) causal_iv_sargan_test(soil_worse, "ph", "yield",                       instruments = c("carbonate", "quarry_km"))$p #> [1] 0.9240283 causal_iv_fit_2sls(soil_worse, "ph", "yield",                    instruments = c("carbonate", "quarry_km"))$effect #> [1] 2.934698

code: if (requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)) {   kg <- causal_kg_new()   kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(     kg, "Mean annual precipitation", "SOC stock",     source     = "Jenny 1941",     evidence   = "Moisture regulates decomposition rate.",     confidence = 0.80   )    # Node labels are normalised to lower-snake-case before insertion,   # so free-text variants collapse onto one node. Convenient for LLM   # output, but it silently merges concepts whose labels differ only   # in case, spaces or hyphens.   kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(     kg, "mean-annual-precipitation", "soc stock",     source     = "Minasny et al. 2017",     evidence   = "Wetter sites accumulate more carbon.",     confidence = 0.55   )   nrow(causal_kg_edges(kg))  # 1 -- the second call merged into the first    # A merge keeps the MAXIMUM confidence and pastes provenance with   # " | ". A weaker second citation can therefore never lower an   # edge's confidence: re-asserting a claim only ever strengthens it.   causal_kg_edges(kg)[, c("source", "confidence")]    # A cycle is only warned about; the edge is still added and the   # graph stops being a DAG, which breaks backdoor adjustment later.   cyclic <- suppressWarnings(     causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "soc stock", "mean annual precipitation",                        confidence = 0.40)   )   igraph::is_dag(cyclic$graph)  # FALSE    # A self-loop is a hard error instead -- and after normalisation   # these two spellings are the same node.   try(causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "SOC stock", "soc-stock")) } #> Error : Self-loops are not allowed (cause == effect).

code: if (requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)) {   # Node labels the way an LLM extractor really emits them: typos,   # plurals, US spellings, over-specific compounds.   kg <- causal_kg_new()   kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "precipitaton", "soc", source = "A")   kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "aluminum", "root_biomass",                            source = "B")   kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "steeper_slopes", "erosion",                            source = "C")   kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "microbial_biomass", "decomposition",                            source = "D")    print(causal_kg_alignment(kg))    # Two things to read off that table.   #   # `steeper_slopes` stays unmatched. The substring tier only matches   # whole underscore-separated tokens, so the plural "slopes" misses   # "slope", and the nearest vocabulary term is 8 edits away, past   # the default max_distance = 4.   #   # `microbial_biomass` is folded into `biomass` by the substring   # tier, silently merging two different carbon pools. Substring   # matching is lossy; drop the tier when you would rather see a   # node come back unmatched than wrongly matched.   print(causal_kg_alignment(kg, method = c("exact", "fuzzy")))    # Do not repair the misses by loosening the fuzzy cap. At   # max_distance = 8 the fuzzy tier maps `steeper_slopes` onto   # `temperature`, which is worse than no match at all.   causal_kg_alignment(kg, max_distance = 8L) } #>            original     canonical    method distance #> 1      precipitaton precipitation     fuzzy        1 #> 2               soc           soc     exact        0 #> 3          aluminum     aluminium     fuzzy        1 #> 4      root_biomass  root_biomass     exact        0 #> 5    steeper_slopes          <NA>      none       NA #> 6           erosion       erosion     exact        0 #> 7 microbial_biomass       biomass substring       NA #> 8     decomposition decomposition     exact        0 #>            original     canonical method distance #> 1      precipitaton precipitation  fuzzy        1 #> 2               soc           soc  exact        0 #> 3          aluminum     aluminium  fuzzy        1 #> 4      root_biomass  root_biomass  exact        0 #> 5    steeper_slopes          <NA>   none       NA #> 6           erosion       erosion  exact        0 #> 7 microbial_biomass          <NA>   none       NA #> 8     decomposition decomposition  exact        0 #>            original     canonical    method distance #> 1      precipitaton precipitation     fuzzy        1 #> 2               soc           soc     exact        0 #> 3          aluminum     aluminium     fuzzy        1 #> 4      root_biomass  root_biomass     exact        0 #> 5    steeper_slopes   temperature     fuzzy        8 #> 6           erosion       erosion     exact        0 #> 7 microbial_biomass       biomass substring       NA #> 8     decomposition decomposition     exact        0

title: Load a Knowledge Graph from disk — causal_kg_load
code: if (requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)) {   kg <- causal_kg_new()   kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "mean annual precipitation", "ndvi",                            source     = "Jenny 1941",                            evidence   = "Water limits primary production.",                            confidence = 0.90)   kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "ndvi", "soc",                            source     = "Minasny et al. 2017",                            evidence   = "Litter inputs scale with NPP.",                            confidence = 0.85)    f <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")   causal_kg_save(kg, f)    # The round trip is exact down to the per-edge timestamps, so a   # reloaded KG is the same audit trail, not an approximation.   print(identical(causal_kg_edges(kg),                   causal_kg_edges(causal_kg_load(f))))    # Loading REPLAYS causal_kg_add_edge() for every saved edge, and   # the replay is wrapped in suppressWarnings(). A KG that warned   # about a cycle while you built it therefore reloads in silence:   # re-check is_dag() after loading rather than waiting to be told.   cyclic <- suppressWarnings(     causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "soc", "mean annual precipitation",                        confidence = 0.40)   )   g <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")   causal_kg_save(cyclic, g)   print(igraph::is_dag(causal_kg_load(g)$graph))  # FALSE, silently    # The reader is guarded by format_version, so aiming it at some   # other .rds fails loudly instead of half-building a graph.   other <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")   saveRDS(list(cause = "clay", effect = "soc"), other)   try(causal_kg_load(other)) } #> [1] TRUE #> [1] FALSE #> Error : File '/tmp/RtmpNvtEGq/file1f0c9631cd5.rds' does not look like a saved edaphos KG (format_version mismatch).

title: Rank Knowledge-Graph edges by evidence strength — causal_kg_rank_edges
code: # \donttest{ # `causal_kg_*()` needs igraph, a Suggests. `R CMD check --as-cran` # DOES execute \donttest blocks, so this guard is load-bearing: # without it the example errors on any machine lacking igraph. if (requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)) {     kg <- causal_kg_new()     kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "precipitation", "soc",                               source = "Jenny 1941", confidence = 0.9)     kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "precipitation", "soc",                               source = "Minasny 2017", confidence = 0.85)      # Read `mean_confidence` carefully. The two calls above did NOT     # create two rows: causal_kg_add_edge() collapses a repeated     # (cause, effect) pair on insertion, pasting the provenance and     # keeping the MAXIMUM confidence. So the graph holds one edge at     # 0.9, the 0.85 is gone, and the "mean" is taken over that single     # row -- it is 0.9, not the 0.875 you might expect.     nrow(causal_kg_edges(kg))   # 1      r <- causal_kg_rank_edges(kg, by = c("n_sources", "mean_confidence"))     r[, c("n_sources", "mean_confidence", "max_confidence")]      # `n_sources` is recovered by counting the pasted provenance, so     # it does see both citations. But mean_confidence == max_confidence     # by construction after a merge: a weaker corroborating source can     # never pull an edge's confidence down.      # The default `by` includes "agrovoc_support", which needs an     # `alignment` and can trigger a live SPARQL lookup. The explicit     # `by` above is what keeps this example offline. } #>   n_sources mean_confidence max_confidence #> 1         2             0.9            0.9 # }

code: if (requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)) {   kg <- causal_kg_new()   kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "precipitaton", "soc",                            source = "Paper A", confidence = 0.7)   kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "soc_stocks", "soc",                            source = "Paper B", confidence = 0.5)    map <- causal_kg_alignment(kg)   kg2 <- causal_kg_rename(kg, map)    # The typo is repaired: `precipitaton` becomes `precipitation`.   print(causal_kg_edges(kg2)[, c("cause", "effect", "source")])    # Now count the edges. `soc_stocks` aligns onto `soc`, so the edge   # `soc_stocks -> soc` collapses into a self-loop and is dropped   # without a warning: renaming can silently shrink a KG. Always   # compare edge counts before and after.   print(c(before = nrow(causal_kg_edges(kg)),           after  = nrow(causal_kg_edges(kg2))))    # Rows with an NA `canonical` are left untouched, so vetoing one   # bad match by hand is enough to keep its edge alive.   map$canonical[map$original == "soc_stocks"] <- NA   nrow(causal_kg_edges(causal_kg_rename(kg, map))) } #>           cause effect  source #> 1 precipitation    soc Paper A #> before  after  #>      2      1  #> [1] 2

code: if (requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE) &&     requireNamespace("dagitty", quietly = TRUE)) {   kg <- causal_kg_new()   kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "mean annual precipitation", "ndvi",                            confidence = 0.90)   kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "mean annual precipitation", "soc",                            confidence = 0.80)   kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "ndvi", "soc", confidence = 0.85)   kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "clay content", "soc",                            confidence = 0.78)   # A speculative claim the extractor was unsure about.   kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "clay content", "ndvi",                            confidence = 0.40)    dag_hi <- causal_kg_to_dagitty(kg, min_confidence = 0.7)   dag_lo <- causal_kg_to_dagitty(kg, min_confidence = 0.3)   c(hi = nrow(dagitty::edges(dag_hi)),   # 4: clay -> ndvi dropped     lo = nrow(dagitty::edges(dag_lo)))   # 5: it survives    # min_confidence is a modelling decision, not a cosmetic filter.   # Keeping the weak clay -> NDVI edge makes clay content a   # confounder of the NDVI -> SOC effect, so it has to enter the   # adjustment set; dropping it leaves precipitation alone. Same   # evidence base, different estimator.   causal_adjustment_set(dag_hi, "ndvi", "soc", effect = "total")   causal_adjustment_set(dag_lo, "ndvi", "soc", effect = "total")    # Set the bar above every edge and you get a valid but empty DAG   # rather than an error, so check before handing it to an   # estimator.   length(names(causal_kg_to_dagitty(kg, min_confidence = 0.95)))  # 0 } #> [1] 0

Default "https://edaphos.io/kg/". schema_uri Character — IRI eds: schema namespace. Default "https://edaphos.io/schema#". namespaces Named character vector extra prefix bindings declare. Useful want reference external vocabularies (e.g. c(agrovoc = "http://aims.fao.org/aos/agrovoc/")). include_metadata Logical — emit document-level metadata (creation time, edaphos version) prov: statements. title: Export a Knowledge Graph to RDF 1.1 Turtle — causal_kg_to_turtle
text: emitted graph uses following prefixes default (overridable via namespaces): ed:   — edaphos KG namespace (one IRI per node edge). eds:  — edaphos schema namespace (defines eds:Causes, eds:confidence, eds:evidence, eds:source). rdf:, rdfs:, xsd:, prov:, dct: — standard W3C vocabularies. Every node L becomes IRI <base_uri>node/<sanitised_L>; every edge becomes IRI <base_uri>edge/<cause>__<effect> typed rdf:Statement, rdf:subject / rdf:predicate / rdf:object pointing nodes eds:Causes used predicate causal direction. Provenance attached via dct:source (bibliographic identifier) prov:generatedAtTime (timestamp).

title: Export a Knowledge Graph to RDF 1.1 Turtle — causal_kg_to_turtle

code: # \donttest{ # `causal_kg_*()` needs igraph, a Suggests. `R CMD check --as-cran` # DOES execute \donttest blocks, so this guard is load-bearing: # without it the example errors on any machine lacking igraph. if (requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)) {     kg <- causal_kg_new()     kg <- causal_kg_add_edge(kg, "precipitation", "soc",                               source = "Jenny 1941",                               evidence = "Higher precipitation favours SOC.",                               confidence = 0.9)     ttl <- causal_kg_to_turtle(kg)     substr(ttl, 1, 200)      # Write to disk.  The emitter is pure R and this example does     # not parse the result back, so treat "loadable by a triple     # store" as a design intent rather than something demonstrated     # here -- validate with rdflib/Jena against your own consumer.     tf <- tempfile(fileext = ".ttl")     causal_kg_to_turtle(kg, tf) } # }

title: Ingest an abstract into a pedogenetic Knowledge Graph — causal_llm_ingest_abstract
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{   # Ollama needs no credentials, only a reachable server. The hosted   # backends take their key from the environment instead:   # backend = "openai" reads OPENAI_API_KEY, backend = "anthropic"   # reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and both ignore `host`.   abstract <- paste(     "Across 212 Cerrado profiles, mean annual precipitation was the",     "dominant control on topsoil organic carbon, whereas slope",     "position governed erosion losses under conventional tillage."   )    kg <- causal_kg_new()   kg <- causal_llm_ingest_abstract(     kg, abstract,     source  = "Silva et al. 2019",     backend = "ollama", model = "gemma4:latest",     host    = "http://localhost:11434"   )    # The "claims" attribute is what was INSERTED, not what the model   # returned -- anything below `min_confidence` is already gone. To   # audit what was discarded, call causal_llm_extract() yourself.   attr(kg, "claims")    # It also carries the model's own labels, which the graph does not:   # node names are snake_cased on insertion, so a claim about   # "mean annual precipitation" becomes the node   # "mean_annual_precipitation".   causal_kg_edges(kg)$cause    # Trap: min_confidence = 0 does not mean "keep everything". The   # filter is `!is.na(confidence) & confidence >= min_confidence`, so   # a claim whose confidence field the model omitted is dropped at   # every threshold, silently.   kg_all <- causal_llm_ingest_abstract(causal_kg_new(), abstract,                                        source = "Silva et al. 2019",                                        min_confidence = 0)    # Trap: a cause and effect that differ only in spacing or hyphens   # ("soil organic carbon" vs "soil-organic-carbon") pass the JSON   # parser, then collapse onto one node, and causal_kg_add_edge()   # raises "Self-loops are not allowed". That error aborts the whole   # call, so every other claim in the abstract is lost too. Wrap the   # ingest whenever the passages are not hand-checked.   kg <- tryCatch(     causal_llm_ingest_abstract(kg, abstract, source = "Silva 2019"),     error = function(e) {       message("skipped abstract: ", conditionMessage(e))       kg     }   ) } # }

title: Ingest a corpus of abstracts into a Knowledge Graph (resumable) — causal_llm_ingest_corpus
text: Every row's (source, abstract) pair hashed stable filename; cache_dir supplied cached JSON file already exists row, LLM call skipped cached claims replayed KG. Failed rows (malformed JSON, timeouts) retried max_retries times exponential backoff. Progress reporting uses base R's txtProgressBar unless custom progress callback passed. 10 000+ abstracts cache makes workflow operationally possible: re-running function crash picks cache left , warm re-runs near- instantaneous.

title: Ingest a corpus of abstracts into a Knowledge Graph (resumable) — causal_llm_ingest_corpus
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{   corpus <- data.frame(     source = c("Jenny 1941", "Minasny et al. 2017", "Poggio 2021"),     abstract = c(       "Climate governs the accumulation of soil organic matter.",       "Wetter sites accumulate more carbon at equal parent material.",       "A purely descriptive survey of Cerrado profile morphology."     ),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   )    # `cache_dir` is what makes a 10 000-abstract run survivable, so it   # must OUTLIVE the R session. file.path(tempdir(), "cache") looks   # right and is useless here: it is wiped on exit, and the next run   # silently re-spends the whole corpus.   cache <- "cerrado_llm_cache"   kg <- causal_llm_ingest_corpus(     causal_kg_new(), corpus,     cache_dir = cache,     backend   = "ollama",   # "openai" / "anthropic" read their key     host      = "http://localhost:11434"   # from the environment   )    # Each row is keyed by md5("source|abstract"). Re-running after a   # crash replays the stored claims rather than calling the LLM, so   # cached rows cost nothing and an interrupted run is resumable;   # editing one abstract re-queries that row alone.   kg <- causal_llm_ingest_corpus(causal_kg_new(), corpus,                                  cache_dir = cache)    # Claims are cached UNFILTERED, so `min_confidence` is applied when   # they are replayed. Re-thresholding a finished corpus therefore   # costs nothing; only edges change, never the cache.   kg_loose <- causal_llm_ingest_corpus(causal_kg_new(), corpus,                                        cache_dir = cache,                                        min_confidence = 0.3)    # Read "failed" carefully. A row is listed there when it yielded NO   # claims after `max_retries`, so a descriptive abstract that   # correctly produces nothing is reported exactly like a row whose   # LLM call kept erroring. It is not a list of network failures.   attr(kg, "failed")    # Supplying `progress` replaces the default txtProgressBar, which   # is only shown for corpora of five rows or more.   kg <- causal_llm_ingest_corpus(     causal_kg_new(), corpus, cache_dir = cache,     progress = function(i, n, source)       message(sprintf("[%d/%d] %s", i, n, source))   ) } # }

title: Live AGROVOC alignment for a vector of free-text terms — causal_ontology_agrovoc_align
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{   # Live SPARQL over HTTP: one round trip per uncached term, several   # seconds each. Point `cache_path` at a location that survives the   # session -- tempdir() is a fresh directory every time R starts, so   # a cache written there never gets read back.   cache <- "tools/.agrovoc_cache.rds"   ag <- causal_ontology_agrovoc_align(     c("soil organic carbon", "bulk density", "gibbsite"),     cache_path = cache, verbose = TRUE   )   ag    # `distance` is the Levenshtein distance between the AGROVOC pref   # label and the query, not a confidence. Zero means the label   # repeats the query verbatim; a large value means AGROVOC returned   # a much longer label that merely contains the query as a   # substring. Filter on it before trusting the mapping.   subset(ag, !is.na(uri) & distance <= 3)    # Failures are cached as well as hits, so an endpoint outage is   # persisted as a permanent NA row and later runs will not retry it.   # Delete the cache file after an outage.   unlink(cache)    # unique() is applied before the terms are lower-cased and trimmed,   # so two spellings of one concept both survive it and the result   # gains a duplicate row (only one query is sent -- the in-flight   # cache absorbs the second). De-duplicate yourself if the row count   # matters downstream.   nrow(causal_ontology_agrovoc_align(c("gibbsite", "Gibbsite"))) } # }

code: vocab <- causal_ontology_cerrado() nrow(vocab) #> [1] 58 table(vocab$category) #>  #>       chemistry         climate         outcome parent_material         process  #>              13               8               5               9               7  #>          relief      vegetation  #>               6              10   # The vocabulary is deliberately narrow: it covers the drivers that # actually turn up in Cerrado pedology abstracts, not all of soil # science. Terms outside it come back unmatched from # causal_kg_alignment() -- that is the intended behaviour, not a bug. # # Note what "narrow" does and does not mean. `gibbsite` and `cec` # ARE in it, because Cerrado abstracts discuss them; the SPELLING # is what is narrow. `cation_exchange_capacity` is absent even # though `cec` is present, so an extractor that emits the expanded # form goes unmatched while one that emits the abbreviation does # not. `salinity` is genuinely out of scope for the biome. c("gibbsite", "cec", "cation_exchange_capacity", "salinity") %in%   vocab$term   # TRUE TRUE FALSE FALSE #> [1]  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE  # A trap: `soc` and `soil_organic_carbon` are BOTH canonical terms, # both filed under chemistry. Alignment will therefore keep them as # two separate nodes rather than merging them -- collapse them # yourself with causal_kg_rename() if your KG needs one carbon node. subset(vocab, term %in% c("soc", "soil_organic_carbon", "soc_loss")) #>                   term  category #> 26                 soc chemistry #> 27 soil_organic_carbon chemistry #> 56            soc_loss   outcome  # Spelling is British throughout, so American labels can only be # rescued by the fuzzy tier of causal_kg_alignment(). grep("alumin|mineralis", vocab$term, value = TRUE) #> [1] "aluminium"      "mineralisation"

title: Sensitivity analysis of an edaphos_causal_iv fit — causal_sensitivity_from_iv
code: # A liming trial where the ASSIGNED rate was randomised but the # APPLIED rate was not: growers on clay-rich plots limed more, and # clay content raises SOC on its own.  Clay is never measured; the # assigned rate is the instrument. set.seed(42) n        <- 400 clay     <- stats::rnorm(n) assigned <- stats::rnorm(n) applied  <- 0.8 * assigned + 0.9 * clay + stats::rnorm(n) soc      <- 1.5 * applied + 1.2 * clay + stats::rnorm(n) trial    <- data.frame(assigned, applied, soc)  ols <- lm(soc ~ applied, data = trial) iv  <- causal_iv_fit_2sls(trial, exposure = "applied",                           outcome = "soc", instruments = "assigned")  # OLS is biased upwards (1.922 against a true effect of 1.5) and # 2SLS recovers 1.533.  Now compare the two robustness values. pick <- c("effect", "se", "rv") round(rbind(   ols = unlist(causal_sensitivity_from_lm(ols, "applied")[pick]),   iv  = unlist(causal_sensitivity_from_iv(iv)[pick]) ), 3) #>     effect    se    rv #> ols  1.922 0.043 0.855 #> iv   1.533 0.098 0.535  # Trap: the RV rewards precision, not correctness.  The confounded # OLS estimate scores 0.855 and the consistent 2SLS estimate only # 0.535, purely because instrumenting more than doubled the standard # error.  Read this wrapper's RV as "how much confounding survives # the instruments", never as a ranking of the two estimators.  # The one structural difference from the `lm` wrapper is the # recorded estimator label. causal_sensitivity_from_iv(iv)$fit_estimator #> [1] "2SLS"

title: Sensitivity analysis of an lm backdoor fit — causal_sensitivity_from_lm
code: data(br_cerrado)  # Effect of dry-season greenness on topsoil carbon, holding the # usual climate/terrain backdoor set fixed. fit <- lm(soc ~ ndvi + map_mm + elev + slope, data = br_cerrado) s <- causal_sensitivity_from_lm(fit, "ndvi") round(c(effect = s$effect, t = s$t_stat,         rv = s$rv, rv_alpha = s$rv_alpha), 3) #>   effect        t       rv rv_alpha  #>   29.840   15.448    0.290    0.258   # RV = 0.290 reads: an unobserved confounder -- soil texture, say -- # would have to explain 29% of the residual variance of `ndvi` AND # 29% of the residual variance of `soc`, on top of the three # covariates, before the coefficient reached zero.  `rv_alpha` # (0.258) is always the smaller of the two: it only has to reach # statistical insignificance, not zero.  # Trap: the RV depends on the fit only through |t| and df, so it is # blind to the units of the exposure.  Rescaling rainfall from mm to # metres multiplies the coefficient by 1000 and leaves the RV where # it was -- a numerically larger effect is not a more robust one. cerrado_m <- br_cerrado cerrado_m$map_m <- cerrado_m$map_mm / 1000 mm <- causal_sensitivity_from_lm(   lm(soc ~ map_mm + ndvi + elev + slope, data = br_cerrado), "map_mm") m <- causal_sensitivity_from_lm(   lm(soc ~ map_m + ndvi + elev + slope, data = cerrado_m), "map_m") round(c(rv_mm = mm$rv, rv_m = m$rv,         effect_ratio = m$effect / mm$effect), 4) #>        rv_mm         rv_m effect_ratio  #>       0.3015       0.3015    1000.0000

title: Bias-adjustment grid for a Cinelli & Hazlett sensitivity contour — causal_sensitivity_grid
code: # A backdoor fit of `soc` on mean annual rainfall in `br_cerrado` # gives beta = 0.008583 g/kg per mm, SE = 0.000529, df = 2020. s <- causal_sensitivity_summary(0.008583, 0.000529, 2020)  # The grid is the contour map that the robustness value summarises. # Evaluate it out to r2_max = RV and the far corner of the # equal-confounding diagonal lands exactly on zero. corner <- causal_sensitivity_grid(0.008583, 0.000529, 2020,                                   grid_size = 2L, r2_max = s$rv) corner[, c("r2_xu_z", "r2_yu_xz", "adjusted_estimate")] #>     r2_xu_z  r2_yu_xz adjusted_estimate #> 1 0.0000000 0.0000000          0.008583 #> 2 0.3016734 0.0000000          0.008583 #> 3 0.0000000 0.3016734          0.008583 #> 4 0.3016734 0.3016734          0.000000  # The two axes are not interchangeable.  `r2_xu_z` enters the bias # factor as r2 / (1 - r2), so confounding of the EXPOSURE bites # harder: the (0.5, 0.2) cell has already flipped the sign of the # estimate while (0.2, 0.5) is still positive. g <- causal_sensitivity_grid(0.008583, 0.000529, 2020,                              grid_size = 6L, r2_max = 0.5) g[(g$r2_xu_z == 0.5 & g$r2_yu_xz == 0.2) |   (g$r2_xu_z == 0.2 & g$r2_yu_xz == 0.5), ] #>    r2_xu_z r2_yu_xz adjusted_estimate        bias bias_factor #> 18     0.5      0.2     -0.0020497684 0.010632768   0.4472136 #> 33     0.2      0.5      0.0001770585 0.008405941   0.3535534  # Sign reversal is not an error: `adjusted_estimate` is the estimate # pushed towards zero by `bias`, and beyond the RV it overshoots. # Ten of these 36 cells come back negative. sum(g$adjusted_estimate < 0) #> [1] 10  # The default is 51 x 51 = 2601 rows, which is the long-format frame # you hand to contour() or ggplot2::geom_contour(). nrow(causal_sensitivity_grid(0.008583, 0.000529, 2020)) #> [1] 2601

title: Structure learning from horizon data -> Knowledge Graph — causal_structure_learn
text: "hc" (default) Hill-climbing greedy search DAG space maximising Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) score (Gaussian BIC continuous variables). Deterministic, fast, widely used. title: Train a tiny DDPM on a collection of soil-map patches — dm_fit
code: # \donttest{ data(br_cerrado)  # br_cerrado is a 45 x 45 grid, so it reshapes into an image.  Model # `twi`: a generative model can only learn structure the field # actually has, and `soc` in this grid carries far less short-range # structure than `twi` does. as_grid <- function(v) {   ux <- sort(unique(br_cerrado$x)); uy <- sort(unique(br_cerrado$y))   m <- matrix(NA_real_, 45L, 45L)   m[cbind(match(br_cerrado$x, ux), match(br_cerrado$y, uy))] <- v   m } lag1 <- function(z) (cor(as.vector(z[, -ncol(z)]), as.vector(z[, -1])) +                      cor(as.vector(z[-nrow(z), ]), as.vector(z[-1, ]))) / 2 round(c(soc = lag1(as_grid(br_cerrado$soc)),         twi = lag1(as_grid(br_cerrado$twi))), 3) #>   soc   twi  #> 0.230 0.785   field  <- as_grid(br_cerrado$twi) field  <- (field - mean(field)) / sd(field) starts <- seq(1L, 38L, by = 5L) cells  <- expand.grid(r = starts, c = starts) stack  <- array(0, dim = c(nrow(cells), 8L, 8L)) for (i in seq_len(nrow(cells)))   stack[i, , ] <- field[cells$r[i]:(cells$r[i] + 7L),                         cells$c[i]:(cells$c[i] + 7L)]  fit <- dm_fit(stack, T = 50L, epochs = 150L, hidden = 32L,               lr = 0.02, seed = 1L) fit #> <edaphos_dm_fit>  (Pilar 9 -- Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model) #>   patch shape : 8 x 8 #>   n_train     : 64   cond_dim = 0 #>   T (steps)   : 50   hidden = 32 #>   initial loss = 2.746  final loss = 0.9268  # The score-matching target is standard normal, so a denoiser that # predicts nothing at all -- eps_theta == 0 -- scores exactly 1. # That is what the training loss must be read against, and the gap # here is small. round(c(initial = fit$history[1L],         final   = fit$history[length(fit$history)],         eps_hat_zero = 1), 4) #>      initial        final eps_hat_zero  #>       2.7463       0.9268       1.0000   # Nor does the gap close with training: `backend = "r"` fits a # readout over frozen random features (an ELM), and that readout has # already converged.  2.7 times the epochs buys 0.05. fit_long <- dm_fit(stack, T = 50L, epochs = 400L, hidden = 32L,                    lr = 0.02, seed = 1L) round(c(epochs_150 = fit$history[150L],         epochs_400 = fit_long$history[400L]), 4) #> epochs_150 epochs_400  #>     0.9268     0.8753   # And the patches overlap by construction (stride 5, window 8), so # these 64 are nowhere near 64 independent training examples. c(n_patches = dim(stack)[1L], H = dim(stack)[2L], W = dim(stack)[3L]) #> n_patches         H         W  #>        64         8         8  # }

title: Sample new soil-map patches from a trained DDPM — dm_sample
code: # \donttest{ data(br_cerrado)  as_grid <- function(v) {   ux <- sort(unique(br_cerrado$x)); uy <- sort(unique(br_cerrado$y))   m <- matrix(NA_real_, 45L, 45L)   m[cbind(match(br_cerrado$x, ux), match(br_cerrado$y, uy))] <- v   m } lag1 <- function(z) (cor(as.vector(z[, -ncol(z)]), as.vector(z[, -1])) +                      cor(as.vector(z[-nrow(z), ]), as.vector(z[-1, ]))) / 2  field  <- as_grid(br_cerrado$twi) field  <- (field - mean(field)) / sd(field) starts <- seq(1L, 38L, by = 5L) cells  <- expand.grid(r = starts, c = starts) stack  <- array(0, dim = c(nrow(cells), 8L, 8L)) for (i in seq_len(nrow(cells)))   stack[i, , ] <- field[cells$r[i]:(cells$r[i] + 7L),                         cells$c[i]:(cells$c[i] + 7L)]  fit <- dm_fit(stack, T = 50L, epochs = 150L, hidden = 32L,               lr = 0.02, seed = 1L) gen <- dm_sample(fit, n_samples = 8L, seed = 7L) dim(gen) #> [1] 8 8 8  # "They look plausible" is not a result.  A generative model of a # spatial field makes a checkable promise: the SPATIAL STATISTICS of # its draws should match the data's.  Two numbers catch the usual # failure modes, and they have to be read together. stat <- function(a) c(sd = mean(apply(a, 1L, sd)),                       lag1 = mean(apply(a, 1L, lag1))) round(rbind(real = stat(stack), generated = stat(gen)), 3) #>              sd   lag1 #> real      0.590  0.322 #> generated 3.169 -0.055  # The draws are five times over-dispersed AND spatially incoherent # (lag-1 near zero against 0.32 in the data).  With `backend = "r"` # the denoiser is a readout over frozen random features and has # learned a marginal scale, not a landscape: these are not soil # maps.  Use `backend = "torch"` for anything you would publish -- # and run this same two-number check on it rather than trusting it.  # `conditioning` is silently IGNORED when the fit was # unconditional: cond_dim is 0, so there is no input for it to # enter through, and the draws are bit-identical to the ones above. same <- dm_sample(fit, n_samples = 8L,                   conditioning = matrix(99, 8L, 1L), seed = 7L) identical(same, gen) #> [1] TRUE  # Conditioning has to be supplied at fit time, and its effect judged # against the signal available.  Patch-mean elevation is nearly # perfectly anti-correlated with patch-mean twi in this grid: elev <- as_grid(br_cerrado$elev) cond <- matrix(0, nrow(cells), 1L) for (i in seq_len(nrow(cells)))   cond[i, 1L] <- mean(elev[cells$r[i]:(cells$r[i] + 7L),                            cells$c[i]:(cells$c[i] + 7L)]) cond[, 1L] <- as.vector(scale(cond[, 1L])) round(cor(cond[, 1L], apply(stack, 1L, mean)), 3) #> [1] -0.997  # ... and yet swinging the conditioner across 3 sd moves the sample # mean by an eighth of the draw-to-draw spread, in the wrong # direction.  Read it as a demonstration of the interface, not of a # calibrated conditional simulator. fit_c <- dm_fit(stack, conditioning = cond, T = 50L, epochs = 150L,                 hidden = 32L, lr = 0.02, seed = 1L) lo <- dm_sample(fit_c, n_samples = 8L,                 conditioning = matrix(-1.5, 8L, 1L), seed = 3L) hi <- dm_sample(fit_c, n_samples = 8L,                 conditioning = matrix(1.5, 8L, 1L), seed = 3L) round(c(mean_low = mean(lo), mean_high = mean(hi),         response = mean(hi) - mean(lo),         draw_sd  = sd(apply(lo, 1L, mean))), 3) #>  mean_low mean_high  response   draw_sd  #>    -0.212    -0.180     0.032     0.260  # }

text: 1. Causal AI. DAG-backed backdoor adjustment via dagitty — causal_clorpt_dag(), causal_cerrado_dag(), causal_adjustment_set(), causal_estimate_effect() — optional non-linear BART estimator via dbarts Suggests dependency. Corpus ingestion clients SciELO (causal_corpus_scielo()) OpenAlex (causal_corpus_openalex()) transparently page upstream APIs multi-thousand-abstract pulls, deduplicated DOI / title via causal_corpus_deduplicate(). Production-grade ingestion corpora tens thousands abstracts handled causal_llm_ingest_corpus()'s cache_dir max_retries arguments (resumable, idempotent, exponential backoff). Ontology alignment curated Cerrado vocabulary live FAO AGROVOC SPARQL (causal_ontology_agrovoc_align(), causal_kg_alignment(vocab = "agrovoc")) provided -disk caching, concurrent batched alignment (causal_ontology_agrovoc_align_batch()) dispatches max_active parallel HTTP requests 10 k-node KG resolves minutes instead hours. Paper-scale KGs persisted audited via causal_kg_save() / causal_kg_load() (portable RDS edge-list), causal_kg_to_turtle() (W3C RDF 1.1 Turtle export reified provenance per edge), causal_kg_rank_edges() (multi-source ranking n_sources + mean_confidence + agrovoc_support) summary() method reports node / edge / source counts, confidence distribution DAG-ness. Multi-extractor voting (causal_llm_vote(), causal_llm_ingest_abstract_voted()) runs N LLM backends abstract resolves disagreements majority, weighted intersection rules. Bottom-structure learning (causal_structure_learn()) recovers DAG directly horizon data bnlearn bridge (hc, tabu, pc-stable, mmhc) optional bootstrap edge confidence, producing edaphos_causal_kg can unioned LLM-derived Knowledge Graph. 2. Physics-Informed ML. Parametric pedogenetic Ordinary Differential Equation, solved closed form fitted horizon-average observation operator — piml_profile_fit(); Neural ODE differentiable Runge-Kutta integrator torch — piml_neural_ode_fit(); hierarchical covariate-conditioned Neural ODE jointly fit across pedons — piml_hierarchical_fit(). Bayesian posterior \((\lambda_0, \mu, y_\infty, y_0)\) returned piml_profile_fit_bayesian() via Laplace approximation (default) adaptive random-walk Metropolis sampler. Neural-ODE variant paired piml_neural_ode_fit_ensemble(), deep ensemble whose empirical spread approximates Bayesian predictive posterior extra torch machinery. 3. 4D Pedometry. Multi-layer stacked Convolutional LSTM sequence--one sequence--sequence training — temporal_convlstm_fit(); multi-step rollout forecasting — temporal_convlstm_rollout(); optional mass-balance physics loss; reproducible synthetic SOC dynamics cube generator — temporal_synth_soc_cube(). 4. Foundation Models. SimCLR scaffold (foundation_simclr_pretrain(), foundation_simclr_embed()) plus MoCo v2 upgrade (foundation_moco_pretrain(), foundation_moco_embed()) momentum encoder, dictionary queue raster-specific augmentation stack. planetary-scale tile pipeline (foundation_tile_source_soilgrids(), foundation_tile_source_worldclim(), foundation_tile_source_srtm(), foundation_tile_align(), foundation_tile_dataset()) streams patches lazily multi-source terra::SpatRaster mosaics; foundation_moco_pretrain_tiles() trains checkpointing -device dispatch (device = "cpu" | "mps" | "cuda"), foundation_moco_embed_raster() projects trained encoder entire AoI. downstream fine-tuning API (foundation_fit_classifier(), foundation_fit_regressor()) wraps head construction, training loop, validation split target normalisation behind single call supports linear probing full fine-tuning two-group learning-rate schedule. Public pretrained weights distributed via Zenodo: foundation_weights_list() catalogues registry, foundation_weights_download() fetches artefact SHA-256 verification caches tools::R_user_dir("edaphos"), foundation_weights_load() rebuilds edaphos_foundation_moco wrapper saved state dict. 5. Autonomous Active Learning. Closed-loop sampling policy combining Quantile-Regression-Forest uncertainty, feature-space diversity logistical cost — al_loop(), al_query(), al_initial_design(), al_fit(), al_update(); global per-location Physics- Informed rejection gates — al_physics_gate_piml(), al_physics_gate_piml_hierarchical(). Information-theoretic batch acquisition provided al_query_batchbald(), maximises mutual information batch model parameters via greedy log-det submodular objective (Kirsch, van Amersfoort Gal 2019). 6. Quantum ML. Pure-R state-vector simulator ZZFeatureMap encoding (Havlicek et al., 2019) quantum-kernel Gram matrix quantum_kernel() closed-form Kernel Ridge Regression wrapper quantum_krr_fit(). full Qiskit-backed Variational Quantum Eigensolver bridge (quantum_hamiltonian(), quantum_hamiltonian_h2(), quantum_hamiltonian_organo_mineral(), quantum_vqe_fit(), quantum_vqe_exact()) runs qiskit-aer box three interchangeable back ends: exact statevector, shot-based Aer SPSA optional noise models, full IBM Quantum Runtime dispatch (quantum_ibmq_submit(), quantum_ibmq_available(), quantum_ibmq_backends(), quantum_ibmq_least_busy()) M3 readout ZNE gate-folding mitigation (Kim et al., 2023). qiskit-nature bridge (quantum_hamiltonian_from_pyscf(), quantum_hamiltonian_organo_mineral_nature(), quantum_nature_total_energy()) lifts user-supplied XYZ geometry PySCF RHF reference, frozen-core reduction, ActiveSpace projection ParityMapper Z2 tapering, producing qubit Hamiltonian ready VQE minimisation. Curated presets cover three canonical organo-mineral motifs: carboxylate ("formic_acid"), ortho-diol ("methanediol"), monodentate Fe(III)– carboxylate coordination complex ("ferric_formate"). 7. Bayesian Hierarchical Spatial. Hierarchical spatial linear model \(y = X\beta + w + \varepsilon\) Gaussian-process random effect \(w \sim GP(0, \sigma^2     \rho(\cdot; \phi))\) — bhs_fit(). \(\beta\) variance updates conjugate therefore closed-form; range \(\phi\) profiled user-supplied grid maximum likelihood, keeps whole sampler free Metropolis steps. Cholesky-heavy inner loop runs RcppArmadillo backend. predict() performs Bayesian kriging unobserved sites, propagating every posterior draw predictive distribution rather plugging point estimate. 8. Neural Operators. Learns solution operator \(\mathcal{G}: u(z) \mapsto y(z)\) depth-function spaces instead pointwise regression. 1-D Fourier Neural Operator (no_fno_fit()) applies \((\mathcal{K}v)(z) = \mathcal{F}^{-1}(R_\theta \cdot     \mathcal{F}v)(z)\) spectrum truncated n_modes (Li et al., 2021); DeepONet (no_deeponet_fit()) factorises \(\mathcal{G}(u)(z) \approx \sum_k b_k(u) t_k(z)\) branch trunk networks (Lu et al., 2021), constructive form Chen Chen (1995) universal operator approximation theorem. expose pure-R backend torch backend full autograd "cpu" / "mps" / "cuda" dispatch. 9. Diffusion Models. Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (Ho, Jain Abbeel, 2020) soil-map patches. dm_cosine_schedule() builds forward process \(q(x_t \mid x_0) = N(\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t} x_0, (1 -     \bar\alpha_t) )\) cosine schedule Nichol Dhariwal (2021); dm_fit() trains denoiser \(\epsilon_\theta(x_t, t)\) score matching; dm_sample() runs ancestral sampling \(t = T\) 0, optionally conditioned covariates. backend = "r" trainer updates readout layer randomly initialised hidden features — Extreme-Learning-Machine regime (Huang, Zhu Siew, 2006) — whereas backend = "torch" trains full network. 10. Graph Neural Networks. Graph Attention Network (Veličković et al., 2018) k-NN co-location graph profiles — gnn_build_graph(), edges = "spatial", "feature" "hybrid" optional self-loops. gnn_fit() trains multi-head attention \(\alpha_{ij} = \mathrm{softmax}_j(\mathrm{LeakyReLU}(     ^\top [W h_i \Vert W h_j]))\) analytic reverse-mode gradients grouped softmax — checked central finite differences test suite — residual connections, head averaging, transductive train_mask test label leaks training, closed-form ridge readout. gnn_fit_ensemble() averages independent seeds published comparison quantile regression forest ensemble-versus-ensemble. gnn_embed() returns learned node embeddings gnn_causal_discovery() hands Pillar 1's structure learner.

code: obs   <- c(12.1, 18.4,  9.7, 22.0, 15.3) pred  <- c(11.5, 19.2, 10.4, 20.8, 15.9)  # The achievable null: the mean of the training fold, known before the # test rows are seen. edaphos_nse(obs, pred, null_prediction = 14.8) #> [1] 0.966548  # The oracle null, which is what edaphos_r2() uses. It is the harder bar, # because the mean of the test set is the best constant predictor OF the # test set -- so a method can clear the achievable null and fail this one. edaphos_nse(obs, pred, null_prediction = mean(obs)) #> [1] 0.9656934 edaphos_r2(obs, pred) #> [1] 0.9656934  # A method that beats the training mean but not the test mean: exactly the # case that gets mislabelled when the two are conflated. round(c(achievable = edaphos_nse(obs, pred, 14.8),         oracle     = edaphos_nse(obs, pred, mean(obs))), 3) #> achievable     oracle  #>      0.967      0.966

title: Unified posterior object for the edaphos pillars — edaphos_posterior
code: # Both posteriors below are built from synthetic random draws, so # set.seed() is what makes the printed summaries reproducible. # They illustrate the container only -- neither is a fitted model. # A real `method = "bootstrap"` posterior comes from the Pillar-1 # block bootstrap, a real `method = "gaussian"` one from the # Pillar-6 QKRR posterior variance; both are obtained by calling # `as_edaphos_posterior()` on that pillar's fit, not by hand. set.seed(42)  # From a posterior sample: 100 draws over a 2-cell query. The draws # are standard normal noise, so this posterior is centred on ~0 with # sd ~1 and would imply no detectable effect at all. post <- edaphos_posterior(   samples    = matrix(stats::rnorm(200), nrow = 100, ncol = 2),   method     = "bootstrap",   query_type = "effect",   units      = "g/kg per mm" ) post #> <edaphos_posterior> #>   method      : bootstrap #>   query_type  : effect #>   units       : g/kg per mm #>   n_samples   : 100 #>   query shape : 2 #>   mean range  : [-0.0875, +0.0325]  mean = -0.0275 #>   sd   range  : [+0.9042, +1.0414]  mean = +0.9728 # Under set.seed(42) the two summary lines printed above read #   mean range  : [-0.0875, +0.0325]  mean = -0.0275 #   sd   range  : [+0.9042, +1.0414]  mean = +0.9728  # From a Gaussian summary. `mean` and `sd` are stored verbatim, but # the constructor still draws `n_samples_if_gaussian` (500) samples # so that uncertainty_calibrate() and autoplot() have a sample to # work with -- that hidden draw is the other thing set.seed() fixes. post2 <- edaphos_posterior(   mean       = c(0.5, 0.7),   sd         = c(0.1, 0.2),   method     = "gaussian",   query_type = "param" ) post2 #> <edaphos_posterior> #>   method      : gaussian #>   query_type  : param #>   n_samples   : 500 #>   query shape : 2 #>   mean range  : [+0.5000, +0.7000]  mean = +0.6000 #>   sd   range  : [+0.1000, +0.2000]  mean = +0.1500  # Those synthesised draws only reproduce the requested sd up to # Monte-Carlo error at n = 500: this prints 0.099 and 0.205 against # the requested 0.1 and 0.2. round(apply(post2$samples, 2L, stats::sd), 3L) #> [1] 0.099 0.205  # print() shows the exact mean / sd; summary() adds quantiles, and # those are computed from the synthesised draws, so they move with # the seed even though the mean / sd lines do not. summary(post2) #> <edaphos_posterior> #>   method      : gaussian #>   query_type  : param #>   n_samples   : 500 #>   query shape : 2 #>   mean range  : [+0.5000, +0.7000]  mean = +0.6000 #>   sd   range  : [+0.1000, +0.2000]  mean = +0.1500 #>  #> Quantiles (over query shape): #>   q05   : min=+0.3355  med=+0.3541  max=+0.3727 #>   q50   : min=+0.4963  med=+0.5995  max=+0.7027 #>   q95   : min=+0.6521  med=+0.8432  max=+1.0342

code: # `output_dir` is DELETED before it is written -- never point it at a # directory that holds anything else.  Everything here stays inside # tempdir(); suppressMessages() only hides the two [zenodo] progress # lines the function prints. out <- file.path(tempdir(), "edaphos-zenodo-demo") dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE) writeLines("not a release artefact", file.path(out, "keep_me.txt"))  # include_tarball = FALSE skips devtools::build(), which compiles the # package found in getwd() rather than anything in `output_dir`; zip = # FALSE skips utils::zip(), which needs a zip binary on the PATH. suppressMessages(   edaphos_zenodo_release(out, include_tarball = FALSE, zip = FALSE)) file.exists(file.path(out, "keep_me.txt"))     # FALSE -- unlink() ran #> [1] FALSE  # Every shipped inst/extdata artefact is copied under bundles/. shipped <- list.files(system.file("extdata", package = "edaphos"),                       pattern = "[.](rds|jsonl)$") c(shipped = length(shipped),   copied  = length(list.files(file.path(out, "bundles")))) #> shipped  copied  #>      34      34   # manifest.csv carries a size and a SHA-256 per file -- but it is # written from a snapshot taken before itself and before # ZENODO-README.md exist, so the table advertised as "checksums for # every file" is missing exactly those two. man <- read.csv(file.path(out, "manifest.csv")) c(rows = nrow(man), files = length(list.files(out, recursive = TRUE))) #>  rows files  #>    37    39  setdiff(list.files(out, recursive = TRUE), man$path) #> [1] "ZENODO-README.md" "manifest.csv"      # The checksums are real, though: recompute one and compare. if (requireNamespace("digest", quietly = TRUE)) {   i <- match("bundles/pilar10_gat_tuning.rds", man$path)   print(identical(man$sha256[i],                   digest::digest(file = file.path(out, man$path[i]),                                  algo = "sha256"))) } else {   print(all(is.na(man$sha256)))   # without digest the column is NA } #> [1] TRUE  # metadata.json is the DataCite block to paste into the Zenodo form. # Its `version` is packageVersion("edaphos") -- the INSTALLED package -- # while a tarball built with include_tarball = TRUE comes from the # DESCRIPTION in getwd().  Install the checkout before you release from # it, or the deposit metadata can name a different version than the # tarball beside it. meta <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(out, "metadata.json")) unlist(meta$metadata[c("upload_type", "access_right", "license")]) #>  upload_type access_right      license  #>   "software"       "open"        "mit"  identical(meta$metadata$version, as.character(packageVersion("edaphos"))) #> [1] TRUE  # CITATION.cff, NEWS.md and README.md are snapshotted only if they can # be found -- first in getwd(), then in the installed package -- so a # bundle built outside a source checkout can be missing them.  Check # before uploading. intersect(c("CITATION.cff", "NEWS.md", "README.md"), list.files(out)) #> [1] "NEWS.md"   "README.md"  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # The full deposit: tarball + zip archive.  devtools::build() runs on # the package in the CURRENT working directory, so call this from a # source checkout.  Upload is manual at https://zenodo.org/deposit/new # -- the package never stores a Zenodo token. edaphos_zenodo_release(file.path(tempdir(), "edaphos-zenodo"),                        include_tarball = TRUE, zip = TRUE) } # }

title: Build the Cerrado raster stack for IV / quantum-foundation benchmarks — foundation_build_cerrado_stack
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Needs `terra`, `geodata` and `digest` installed, and a network.  # The default call assembles the 31-layer "v1_encoder" stack over a # 2 deg x 2 deg quadrant around Brasilia at 0.01 deg.  What actually # crosses the wire: five GLOBAL SoilGrids rasters for the 0-5 cm # interval, the whole Brazil WorldClim 2.1 country tiles for `prec` # and `tavg` (12 monthly layers each, cropped only after download -- # this is the dominant cost), and the Brazil SRTM elevation tile. # `slope` is not downloaded: it is derived locally from `elev` with # terra::terrain(). stk <- foundation_build_cerrado_stack() terra::nlyr(stk)             # 31 names(stk)[c(1:5, 30:31)]    # soc clay sand phh2o bdod elev slope  # Every one of those sources is a 30 arc-second (roughly 1 km) # product -- geodata rewrites the SoilGrids URL to end in # "_30s.tif", so the native 250 m SoilGrids never enters this # package.  The 0.01 deg output grid is finer than the data on it; # the resample that put it there is interpolation, not detail. terra::res(stk)              # 0.01 0.01 sg <- geodata::soil_world(var = "soc", depth = 5, vsi = TRUE) terra::sources(sg)           # .../soc_0-5cm_mean_30s.tif terra::res(sg)               # 0.008333333 = 1/120 deg = 30 arc-sec  # The written file is small; the download is not, and both live in # cache_dir.  Measure them instead of trusting either intuition. cache_dir <- tools::R_user_dir("edaphos", which = "cache") assembled <- list.files(cache_dir, pattern = "cerrado_stack_",                         full.names = TRUE) round(file.size(assembled) / 1024^2, 1)   # 200 x 200 x 31 FLT4S: a few MB round(sum(file.size(list.files(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE,                                full.names = TRUE)),           na.rm = TRUE) / 1024^2, 1)      # the raw sources: far larger  # The cache key is (schema, bbox, target_res): `schema` goes into # the file name verbatim and the other two are md5-hashed after it, # giving cerrado_stack_<schema>_<md5>.tif.  A repeat of the same # call touches no network at all and reports "Using cached stack:". stk_again <- foundation_build_cerrado_stack() basename(terra::sources(stk_again))  # A different AoI or resolution is a different key, hence a fresh # download that lands beside the first one rather than replacing it. # `force = TRUE` is the only way to re-fetch and overwrite the file # for a key you have already built; it leaves the other keys alone. stk_small <- foundation_build_cerrado_stack(bbox = c(-49, -15, -48, -14)) stk_fresh <- foundation_build_cerrado_stack(force = TRUE)  # `cache_dir` is handed to geodata as its own download `path`, so # the directory ends up holding the raw SoilGrids / WorldClim / SRTM # rasters as well as the assembled .tif.  Point it at a disk with # room, and reuse the same one across sessions. stk_tmp <- foundation_build_cerrado_stack(   cache_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "edaphos-stacks"))  # "minimal" is not a smaller stack, it is a different one: 10 layers # (soc, clay, sand, phh2o, bdod, bio1, bio12, elev, slope, ndvi) and # no monthly climate at all.  The published v1 encoder's input layer # is fixed at 31 channels -- `foundation_weights_list()` reports # `n_channels` -- so a minimal stack cannot feed it.  It exists to # reproduce the pre-v4.0.0 bundles. legacy <- foundation_build_cerrado_stack(schema = "minimal") terra::nlyr(legacy)          # 10  # If any single source is unreachable, that layer is skipped with a # warning and the function then stops with the list of missing # names, having written nothing: a partially downloaded stack never # reaches the cache, so a failed run cannot be silently inherited by # the next one.  # One exception to that loudness. `elev` is fetched with # geodata::elevation_30s(country = "BRA"), which masks to the # Brazilian border, so an AoI crossing into a neighbour comes back # NA on the far side -- and `slope`, derived from it, with it.  If # that call errors the code falls back to # geodata::elevation_global(res = 0.5): the same 30 arc-seconds, but # WorldClim's elevation product rather than SRTM, and unmasked.  No # warning marks the substitution, and the layer is called `elev` # either way. terra::global(stk[[c("elev", "slope")]], "isNA")  # Downstream: the stack feeds a tile dataset, and the dataset plus a # pretrained encoder give one instrument row per soil profile.  Note # that foundation_tile_dataset() derives the normalisation # statistics from the stack you just built, not from the encoder's # training run -- v1's training means / sds were never persisted # (`foundation_weights_list()` reports `norm_stats_status` as # "unrecoverable"), so this is the documented substitute, not a # match. tiles <- foundation_tile_dataset(stk, patch_size = 16L,                                  n_patches = 2000L, seed = 1) moco  <- foundation_weights_load("edaphos-cerrado-moco-v1") profiles <- data.frame(lon = c(-49.5, -48.7), lat = c(-15.4, -14.6)) emb <- foundation_embed_at_coords(moco, profiles, stk, tiles) dim(emb)                     # 2 x 64 = registry feature_dim for v1  # Unlike foundation_moco_pretrain(), foundation_weights_load() calls # $eval() before handing the encoder over, so the BatchNorm / # batch_size interaction documented in the # foundation_embed_at_coords() example does not apply here.  Check # rather than assume if you built the encoder some other way. moco$encoder_q$training      # FALSE } # }

code: if (requireNamespace("torch", quietly = TRUE) &&     isTRUE(torch::torch_is_installed()) &&     requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)) {    # A 2 deg x 2 deg Cerrado tile at 0.05 deg (40 x 40 cells) with   # three covariate channels, standing in for the 31-channel stack   # that foundation_build_cerrado_stack() downloads.   cerrado <- terra::rast(nrows = 40, ncols = 40,                          xmin = -50, xmax = -48,                          ymin = -16, ymax = -14,                          crs = "EPSG:4326", nlyrs = 3)   xy <- terra::xyFromCell(cerrado, seq_len(terra::ncell(cerrado)))   terra::values(cerrado) <- cbind(     900 + 260 * sin((xy[, 1] + 50) * 2.4) - 140 * (xy[, 2] + 16),     1500 - 90 * (xy[, 1] + 50) + 40 * cos((xy[, 2] + 16) * 3),     0.45 + 0.18 * sin((xy[, 1] + 50) * 1.7 + (xy[, 2] + 16)))   names(cerrado) <- c("elev", "map_mm", "ndvi")    # Touch torch once before relying on `seed`: the call that loads   # the backend does not keep it.   invisible(torch::torch_manual_seed(11L))   set.seed(42)   tiles <- foundation_tile_dataset(cerrado, patch_size = 8L,                                    n_patches = 24L, seed = 1)   moco  <- foundation_moco_pretrain(tiles$sample(12),                                     feature_dim = 8L, proj_dim = 4L,                                     epochs = 2L, batch_size = 6L,                                     seed = 11L)    # Five profiles: three interior, one outside the tile, and one   # inside it but in the very first column of cells.   sites <- data.frame(     site = c("BR-01", "BR-02", "BR-03", "BR-04", "BR-05"),     lon  = c(-49.50, -48.70, -49.10, -46.20, -49.96),     lat  = c(-15.40, -14.60, -15.50, -15.00, -15.40))    # Put the encoder in eval mode before extracting anything.   # foundation_moco_pretrain() hands it back in TRAINING mode and   # the backbone is full of BatchNorm, which in training mode   # standardises with the statistics of the batch in front of it:   # a site's embedding then depends on which other sites share its   # batch, and `batch_size` stops being only a memory knob.   b32 <- foundation_embed_at_coords(moco, sites, cerrado, tiles,                                     batch_size = 32L)   b01 <- foundation_embed_at_coords(moco, sites, cerrado, tiles,                                     batch_size = 1L)   invisible(moco$encoder_q$eval())   e32 <- foundation_embed_at_coords(moco, sites, cerrado, tiles,                                     batch_size = 32L)   e01 <- foundation_embed_at_coords(moco, sites, cerrado, tiles,                                     batch_size = 1L)   # First entry is the size of the leak; the second is zero to   # numerical precision.   print(c(train_mode = max(abs(b32 - b01), na.rm = TRUE),           eval_mode  = max(abs(e32 - e01), na.rm = TRUE)))    # One row per site, in the order supplied, `feature_dim` columns   # named emb_001 ... emb_008.   print(dim(e32))   print(colnames(e32))    # Rows 4 and 5 come back all NA for two different reasons that   # look identical in the output: BR-04 is outside the raster,   # while BR-05 is inside it but a patch centred there would run   # off the western edge.  Carry the site identifiers alongside --   # the matrix has no row names to tell you which is which.   print(cbind(sites["site"], usable = stats::complete.cases(e32)))    # The margin required is exactly `patch_size %/% 2` = 4 cells.   # Marching east from the western edge, the first four columns of   # the raster are refused and the fifth is the first that returns   # an embedding.   transect <- data.frame(lon = -49.975 + 0.05 * (0:5), lat = -15.4)   print(is.na(foundation_embed_at_coords(moco, transect, cerrado,                                          tiles)[, 1]))    # NA is only ever a geometric verdict.  Missing covariate values   # inside the window are imputed at the channel mean, so a site   # sitting on a NoData hole still gets a full embedding row --   # only terra::extract() will tell you it is uninformed.   holed <- cerrado   hole  <- terra::cellFromXY(holed, as.matrix(expand.grid(     lon = -49.10 + c(-0.05, 0, 0.05),     lat = -15.50 + c(-0.05, 0, 0.05))))   vals <- terra::values(holed)   vals[hole, ] <- NA   terra::values(holed) <- vals   emb_holed <- foundation_embed_at_coords(moco, sites, holed, tiles)   # All three covariates are NA at BR-03 (column 1 is terra's ID),   # yet the embedding row is finite.   print(terra::extract(holed, sites[3, c("lon", "lat")]))   print(all(is.finite(emb_holed[3, ])))    # `projection = TRUE` returns the L2-normalised projection head   # instead of the backbone features: `proj_dim` columns, and every   # extracted row has unit length.   proj <- foundation_embed_at_coords(moco, sites, cerrado, tiles,                                      projection = TRUE)   ok <- stats::complete.cases(proj)   print(c(ncol = ncol(proj),           norm = unique(round(sqrt(rowSums(proj[ok, ]^2)), 6)))) }
